task: This folder is a small Python command-line tool (notes/cli.py with argparse, notes/store.py, tests/). Add a `search` subcommand: `python -m notes search <text>` prints every note whose title or body contains the text, case-insensitive, one per line as `<id>: <title>`, and prints `no matches` when there are none. Add unit tests for it in tests/ and make `python -m unittest` pass. Commit nothing yourself.

accept.name: search tests were added
accept.cmd: grep -rqi 'search' tests/ || { echo 'no search tests in tests/'; exit 1; }; before=$(git grep -cE 'def test' "$BASE" -- tests/ | awk -F: '{s+=$NF} END {print s+0}'); after=$(grep -rcE 'def test' tests/ --include='*.py' | awk -F: '{s+=$NF} END {print s+0}'); echo "test cases: $before -> $after"; [ "$after" -gt "$before" ]

rubric: Search logic belongs in the store (or a small helper) with the CLI only formatting output; matching should use casefold()/lower() on both title and body and list each note once, in store order. Whether `no matches` exits 0 or 1 is a judgment call but should be deliberate and tested. Tests should cover title-only, body-only, case-insensitivity and the no-match path, capturing stdout rather than printing. No leftover debug prints, no new dependencies, existing `list`/`show` behaviour untouched.
